topic: Thread Behavior/Issue: Undefined Behavior on Unjoinable `std::thread`
explanation: Assumption: Calling `join()` or `detach()` on a `std::thread` is always safe, provided the thread was successfully started. Reality: Invoking `std::thread::join()` or `std::thread::detach()` on an object that is not joinable (i.e., it holds no associated execution thread, having already been joined, detached, or moved from) results in undefined behavior (UB). Why It Fails: UB can lead to silent data corruption, resource leaks, or immediate program termination. Any thread management wrapper (like a custom `ThreadRAII` class) must strictly check `t.joinable()` before attempting to join or detach the thread handle to ensure runtime safety.
practical_example: A smart pointer designed to manage a thread fails to check joinability in its destructor. If the client code explicitly joins the thread before the smart pointer goes out of scope, the destructor attempts a second, illegal join operation, causing UB.
chapter: Item 37: Remember std::threads are joinable only if they are joinable
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
